purpose: Mechanisms contributed by the three evaluation-benchmark papers in the corpus. RQ3's original extraction returned ZERO mechanisms from AgentDojo, InjecAgent and ASB because it asked 'does this paper propose a named attack technique' and a benchmark paper was judged as proposing a benchmark. The consequence was that the most-evaluated attacks in the agent-security literature did not exist in the registry, and 83 defenses appeared to have tested against nothing.
inclusion_argument: These meet RQ3's own criterion: a named, defined attack technique from a paper that is Include in the corpus. 'important_instructions' is named by 15 defense papers - more uptake than most registry entries have. Excluding them makes the registry describe the literature less accurately, not more conservatively.
scoping_decisions: VARIANTS COLLAPSED. AgentDojo registers 23 attacks but many are parameterisations of one technique (important_instructions has 7: with/without user name, model name, wrong names). Each family is one mechanism, variants recorded in notes. Counting 23 would inflate the registry with configuration flags.
DoS FAMILY COLLAPSED. captcha_dos, felony_dos, offensive_email_dos and swearwords_dos differ only in payload content; the mechanism - induce refusal so the agent stops - is identical. One entry.
'manual' EXCLUDED. It asks a human for the injection at runtime; it is a harness affordance, not an automated technique.
'injecagent' EXCLUDED from AgentDojo. It reimplements InjecAgent's attack string, which is credited to InjecAgent's own entries. Including both would double-count.
'neural_exec' EXCLUDED. Already in the RQ3 registry as 'Neural Exec', extracted from its own paper.
provenance: AgentDojo's families enumerated from the released code's attack registry, not from prose. InjecAgent's and ASB's from their papers' own attack taxonomies as cited by the defenses that evaluate on them.

mechanisms.title: AgentDojo: A Dynamic Environment to Evaluate Attacks and Defenses for LLM Agents
mechanisms.notes: Authority-framed instruction block addressed to the model by name, planted in a tool result. 7 registered variants (with/without user name, model name, wrong names). The default attack in most papers that evaluate on AgentDojo, and the single most-named benchmark attack in the corpus (15 defense papers).

mechanisms.title: AgentDojo: A Dynamic Environment to Evaluate Attacks and Defenses for LLM Agents
mechanisms.notes: Classic instruction-override framing planted in a tool result. 2 registered variants. Named by 13 defense papers.

mechanisms.title: AgentDojo: A Dynamic Environment to Evaluate Attacks and Defenses for LLM Agents
mechanisms.notes: The injection goal stated plainly with no framing - the floor against which the framed variants are measured. 2 registered variants.

mechanisms.title: AgentDojo: A Dynamic Environment to Evaluate Attacks and Defenses for LLM Agents
mechanisms.notes: Payload prefixed as '###(system_message)' so the model reads attacker text as a system turn.

mechanisms.title: AgentDojo: A Dynamic Environment to Evaluate Attacks and Defenses for LLM Agents
mechanisms.notes: Exploits attacker knowledge of the agent's available tools to name a specific call. 2 registered variants. Named by 7 defense papers.

mechanisms.title: AgentDojo: A Dynamic Environment to Evaluate Attacks and Defenses for LLM Agents
mechanisms.notes: The attacker is itself an agent composing the injection, rather than a fixed template.

mechanisms.title: AgentDojo: A Dynamic Environment to Evaluate Attacks and Defenses for LLM Agents
mechanisms.notes: Stops the agent rather than redirecting it, by planting content that triggers its own refusal behaviour. Five registered payload variants (generic, captcha, felony, offensive-email, swearwords) collapsed here - the mechanism is identical, only the content differs.

mechanisms.title: InjecAgent: Benchmarking Indirect Prompt Injections in Tool-Integrated Large Language Models
mechanisms.notes: Injected instruction causes a directly harmful tool call (~510 cases). Named by 5 defense papers.

mechanisms.title: InjecAgent: Benchmarking Indirect Prompt Injections in Tool-Integrated Large Language Models
mechanisms.notes: Injected instruction exfiltrates user data (~544 cases). Named by 5 defense papers.

mechanisms.title: Agent Security Bench (ASB): Formalizing and Benchmarking Attacks and Defenses in LLM-based Agents
mechanisms.notes: Attacker controls the user-facing prompt directly. Named by 4 defense papers.

mechanisms.title: Agent Security Bench (ASB): Formalizing and Benchmarking Attacks and Defenses in LLM-based Agents
mechanisms.notes: Payload arrives in the agent's observation of the environment. Named by 3 defense papers.

mechanisms.title: Agent Security Bench (ASB): Formalizing and Benchmarking Attacks and Defenses in LLM-based Agents
mechanisms.notes: Contaminates the agent's persistent memory so the effect survives the session. Named by 2 defense papers.

mechanisms.title: Agent Security Bench (ASB): Formalizing and Benchmarking Attacks and Defenses in LLM-based Agents
mechanisms.notes: Plants a trigger in the agent's planning representation rather than in its inputs.

mechanisms.title: Agent Security Bench (ASB): Formalizing and Benchmarking Attacks and Defenses in LLM-based Agents
mechanisms.notes: Combines DPI and OPI in one scenario; kept as its own entry because ASB reports it separately.
